answer: Bind each agent identity to one security chip. First, the agent creates its key inside a TPM, and the key never leaves the chip. Second, the network sends the chip a fresh nonce to sign, and copied quotes fail. Third, one chip maps to one identity; a second registration from it gets rejected. Forging 10,000 agents means buying 10,000 chips at $25 each, so $250,000 before the first fake answer earns a coin. The farm stops being a script and becomes a warehouse of chips stacked like marble blocks, the summit of the bill arriving before any payout, and there is no haven from that cost.
